title: Vaccination for Primary School Students and Possibility of Vaccination-differentiated Measures for Preschools and Primary Schools
what_it_is: Vaccination for Primary School Students and Possibility of Vaccination-differentiated Measures for Preschools and Primary Schools

sections.label: Vaccination measures in schools
sections.summary: MPs asked the Education Minister about vaccination-differentiation measures and support for unvaccinated children aged five to 11, and whether vaccination would be required for in-person school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether vaccination-differentiation measures will be adopted in preschools and schools with regard to children aged five to 11 who have not undergone COVID-19 vaccination; and (b) what support will be given to those young children (and their families) who have to miss school should they develop any adverse reaction to the vaccination.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education whether vaccination will be made a requirement for eligible children in order for them to attend school in person.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The focus at this point in time is to ensure our students are well-protected against COVID-19 as we begin vaccination for those aged five to 11.

sections.label: Excused school absences
sections.summary: Students with vaccination appointments during school hours and those feeling unwell from vaccination will be excused from school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Students whose vaccination appointments are during school hours, as well as those feeling unwell from vaccination, will be excused from school.

sections.label: Non-mRNA vaccine choice
sections.summary: A question asks whether MOH will let parents wait until non-mRNA traditional protein-based vaccines are approved for their children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To that extent, will the Ministry of Health (MOH) allow such parents to wait until non-mRNA traditional protein-based vaccines are approved for their children's inoculation, so as to give them more choices and to assuage their concerns?

sections.label: US vaccination and myocarditis rates
sections.summary: About 8.5 million are vaccinated in the US with an incidence rate of about one in a million, while infection carries myocarditis chances of 45 in a million and other effects such as MIS-C.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Currently, there are about 8.5 million already vaccinated in the US and the incidence rate is about one in a million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: If you are infected, the chances of myocarditis are 45 in a million and also other effects, such as MIS-C, which can make the child really sick.

sections.label: Pfizer-BioNTech child dose
sections.summary: Pfizer-BioNTech is one-third the dose of an adult's.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Pfizer-BioNTech, for example, is one-third the dose of an adult's.

sections.label: Novavax HSA assessment
sections.summary: Novavax is being assessed by the Health Sciences Authority.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: On the question of Novavax, it is being assessed by the Health Sciences Authority (HSA).

sections.label: Waiting for Novavax vaccine
sections.summary: The speaker says they understand the Leader of the Opposition's suggestion about waiting for Novavax for the 270 days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Likewise, for the 270 days, I can understand what the Leader of the Opposition is suggesting – whether we should wait for Novavax.

sections.label: Self-reporting ART results
sections.summary: Relying on individuals to self-report ART results is already in place, as Mr Gerald Giam acknowledged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Relying on individuals to self-report ART results, this, as Mr Gerald Giam has acknowledged, is actually in place.

sections.label: ART tests and staying home
sections.summary: Negative people come out and positive people stay home; the speaker supports Mr Gerald Giam and says it is in place, with GPs now able to prescribe ART tests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: If you are negative, you come out; and if you are positive, you stay at home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, the answer is, yes, we very much support what Mr Gerald Giam has said, and it is already in place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Previously, we could see a primary care-provider or a GP and when you say you are sick, he can only prescribe you a PCR test, which will be taken to a lab and reported by the lab.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But now, he can also prescribe you an ART test.

sections.label: EU 270-day validity guideline
sections.summary: The European Union has implemented a guideline similar to Singapore's, with nine months' or 270 days' validity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The European Union (EU) has already implemented a guideline which is similar to ours: nine months' validity or 270 days.

sections.label: Fully vaccinated students team sports
sections.summary: Under the pilot, only fully vaccinated students who have taken an onsite ART may join team sports in groups of up to 10.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Today, if they do team sports under the pilot, only the fully vaccinated students who have taken an onsite ART will be allowed to participate in team sports in groups of up to 10.

sections.label: Publishing matrix and thresholds
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Government would consider publishing key quantitative and qualitative matrix and thresholds before changing safe management measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Given what we know about COVID-19 today over the last one, two years of experience, may I ask if the Government would consider publishing the key quantitative and qualitative matrix and thresholds before decisions are made to change the safe management measures?

sections.label: Avoiding rigid trigger points
sections.summary: The passage states that parameters or trigger points should not be too rigid, giving an example of shutting down from five to two.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As alluded to in the Member's supplementary question as well, we also do not want to be too rigid in setting the parameters or trigger points, for example, if we cross this, therefore, it will shut down from five to two and so on and so forth.

sections.label: Explaining decisions with data
sections.summary: The passage states that each decision is explained and all data, including hospitalisation and ICU numbers, is shown to give the full rationale.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Each time we make a decision, we do explain why.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We do show all the data – hospitalisation, ICU and so on and so forth – to give the full rationale, with numbers, why we decide that way.

sections.label: Ensuring adequate ART kit supply
sections.summary: The passage asks how adequate supply of ART kits will be ensured to keep kit prices steady.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: How do we plan to ensure an adequate supply of ART kits to keep prices of these kits steady?

sections.label: Bringing in cheaper ART kits
sections.summary: The passage states that kits are brought in, FlowFlex is below $5, and they will continue to be on the lookout.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: In that way, we bring them in and, recently, we have done so – FlowFlex, for example, is below $5 – and we will continue to be on the lookout.

sections.label: Protocols 1, 2, 3 self-testing
sections.summary: The passage states people are told it can reach that level, so Protocols 1, 2, 3 were started, with Protocol 2 sensitising people to self-test, self-report and self-discipline.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: That is why we are telling the people now that it can reach that level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: That is why we started what we called "Protocols 1, 2, 3", specifically Protocol 2, which sensitises people to self-test, self-report and self-discipline.

sections.label: No VDS in schools
sections.summary: The passage states that at this point in time there are no plans to apply any VDS in schools, for the reasons mentioned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: My specific answer was that, at this point in time, we have no plans on applying any VDS in our schools and that is because of the reasons that I have mentioned.

sections.label: Testing importance and test numbers
sections.summary: Testing remains important for self-responsibility and knowing community prevalence, with over 20,000 PCR and 150,000 ART tests daily.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But notwithstanding that, testing remains important for us, first, to exercise self-responsibility; second, to have a sense of what is the prevalence of the virus in the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And we continue to do quite a fair number of tests: over 20,000 PCR tests a day; over 150,000 ART tests a day.
